stem: The volume of a rectangular prism is ${=V}\ \text{cm}^{3}$. Its length, its width and its height are all multiplied by ${=k}$. What is the volume of the new prism, in $\text{cm}^{3}$?
solution: All three dimensions of the prism are multiplied by the scale factor $k = {=k}$.
When every length is multiplied by $k$, the volume is multiplied by $k^{3}$. So $k^{3} = {=k}^{3} = {=k ** 3}$.
notes: Basic entry point for the volume rule: whole-number enlargement of all three dimensions, original volume given, new volume asked. Parent ex13-6-5 (every side of a triangular prism quadrupled, volume scales by k^3); the figure shows a triangular prism with b, h, H, and this family uses a rectangular prism with length, width and height so that all three dimensions are named in the stem and nothing is ambiguous. Whole-number answer always (V * k^3, at most 1280). Typical wrong answers are V * k (scale-factor-applied-once) and V * k^2 (wrong-power-for-measure). Numeric family, so no distractor options carry those ids.
